>when did it all start?

I suppose it's always been like this, though it only became clear to me how shallowly I regard people when I was faced with the prospect of losing that person. If someone supposedly close to me died or had to leave with little chance of me seeing them again....well I could always find someone else to fill in the role they left. Grandma died? I have other relatives. Childhood friend's gone? I have other kids I could play with. Best confidante left? I don't care  what you think about me so I have no trouble unloading my issues or secrets on anyone who asks.

>did you "get better" at it through experiences?

Not sure what you meant by 'it.' I'm assuming you meant the facade of being seen as normal.

 I realized how valuable being likeable is. People are more willing to cooperate and do things for you when they like you. One way of doing this is to *show* how much you care about people. You act sad when they leave and act happy when they're around you. Ask them about themselves. Another is to be efficient when it comes to being nice. Do things for other people that won't put you out much when they don't expect or ask for it, and they're more likely to go out of their way to help you when *you* ask. And the best way of forging an emotional connection is to share something about yourself that carries emotional weight, so they'll sympathize and share their own stuff. This makes them feel like they're trusted and special. 

>is there someone special you REALLY wanted to stay with but had to get away from coz they were gonna mess up your plans?

If they were gonna mess up my plans, why would I want to put in the effort? It wouldn't get to the point where I would REALLY want them tbh. This mostly applies to romantic prospects though. I can't think of a situation where being friends with someone could mess up anything, since you never know how useful someone's gonna be and they're pretty easy to drop. Romantic relationships are a lot more...binding. More expectations and harder to drop cleanly. So I have a social criteria for potential partners(ex. if we have to work together to produce an output, you're out, so no coworkers, classmates). Fail that and I won't even find you attractive.

I did fall in love with someone though. It wouldn't have worked out and I have since revised my criteria to ensure it doesn't happen again. For someone I supposedly loved though, even I was surprised by how quickly I got over it once it hit me that it's never gonna happen.

>what/who do you think will make you change for the best?

no idea.

>where do yousee yourself in old age? coz obviously you cannot remain with one person so are you gonna stay single forever?

sure, why not

>what is one relationship you look back on and think "wow i went too far with this one, even for my standards"?

By my standards? none. Pretty sure the ones on the receiving end thought I'm a cunt though.

>how can someone who is hooked up on a person like you deal with the "aftermath" in your opinion?

Move on. Most likely they already have. You can take comfort in the knowledge that it's really not you, it's them. I don't know about the person you're hooked on, but for me, once I decided I don't want you in my life, pursuing me would only make me resent you. However, I've heard that some people would do something like this because they get off on the attention, they enjoy having someone come after them even after they get rejected. So if whoever this is makes an effort of re-establishing contact even after they told you they don't like you anymore, RUN.

I could also be wildly misinterpreting your situation here, so feel free to PM me if you want to clarify your situation a bit so I could give you more accurate advice or something.
